title: OpenAI DevDay 2026 Recap for Developers
gist: At DevDay 2026 OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Sol (near GPT-6 Astra quality at one-fifth the price), computer use in the Agents API, cloud Codex, a Decisions API and persistent agents (Dots, ChatGPT Space), pushing its platform toward persistent agent workflows.

insights.claim: OpenAI's Agents API now supports computer use, letting applications operate software through graphical interfaces, and bundles Codex multi-agent capabilities, tool search, tool calling and context compaction with OpenAI managing the underlying execution infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Managed execution infrastructure pulls agent workloads onto OpenAI's platform, competing with third-party agent frameworks and hosts.

insights.claim: Computer use for the Agents API is available through the API and in Codex and ChatGPT Work for selected plans only, so access is tiered.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Plan gating suggests staged rollout and a monetization lever for higher tiers.

insights.claim: OpenAI is extending its platform from individual model calls toward persistent agents that use tools, operate software, collaborate and execute tasks remotely.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Platform lock-in shifts to agent runtime and workflow layers, not just model quality.
insights.quote: DevDay 2026 showed OpenAI moving beyond individual model interactions toward persistent agent workflows.

insights.claim: OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Sol approaches GPT-6 Astra on several evaluations while charging one-fifth of Astra's standard input and output token prices.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: A roughly 5x price cut at near-frontier quality pressures per-token margins across model vendors and favors high-volume agent use.

insights.claim: GPT-6.1 Sol cached input costs $0.10 per million tokens, and the model targets coding, computer use and professional tasks across the API, ChatGPT Work and Codex.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Cheap cached input makes long-context, agentic loops economically viable.

insights.claim: One developer reacted that GPT-6.1 Sol may be the best release in OpenAI's history, describing 'Luna pricing, Astra-level quality'; this is anecdotal community sentiment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Early developer enthusiasm centers on price-performance rather than raw capability.

insights.claim: Codex can now run in cloud environments as well as locally, letting developers start remote tasks from other devices.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Cloud-run coding agents shift compute and usage toward OpenAI-hosted infrastructure and recurring spend.

insights.claim: The Codex CLI gained voice input and an /agents interface for delegating and monitoring multiple tasks.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Multi-task orchestration UX signals coding moving from single assistant to supervised agent fleets.

insights.claim: OpenAI added a code-review workflow for GitHub pull requests and GitLab merge requests, and Codex Security Cloud that scans repositories and new commits, investigates findings, removes duplicates and prepares fixes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: OpenAI is moving into code review and AppSec, overlapping with security and review tool vendors.

insights.claim: The Decisions API, in limited preview, uses the smaller Luna model to pick from a predefined set of answers based on text or image context, aimed at classification, request routing and choosing an agent's next action.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Cheap constrained-output models for routing become a control-plane primitive for agents and compete with decision-only model startups.

insights.claim: ChatGPT plugins can now provide sidebar experiences, interactive conversation panels and custom file viewers, and respond to events via the proposed MCP Events specification to trigger automations.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Event-driven MCP extends ChatGPT toward an automation platform and raises the stakes for MCP standardization.

insights.claim: DevDay introduced Dots, persistent agents working on ongoing tasks, and ChatGPT Space, a shared workspace for teams and agents with common context.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Shared-context team workspaces target enterprise collaboration seats.

insights.claim: An OpenAI developer predicted Dots would become the favorite way for most people to interact with AI; this is a promotional insider view.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Treat as insider sentiment, not evidence of adoption.
insights.quote: I expect this to become the favorite way of interacting with AI for most people.

insights.claim: Some developers questioned whether the DevDay releases were significant advances over capabilities already available across existing agent platforms, while others praised computer use, cloud Codex and lower-cost models as practical.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Differentiation may rest on price and integration rather than novel capability, a risk for premium valuation of the stack.
